    ingest: add TestDisableWALIngest for regular and flushable ingest paths
    
    Test that ingest works correctly with DisableWAL: true. Two subtests:
    
    - Regular: SST keys don't overlap memtable, so ingest goes directly to
      the LSM. Verifies MemtableOverlappingFiles==0, no WAL bytes written,
      flush is not an ingest-as-flush, and data survives reopen.
    
    - Flushable: SST keys partially overlap memtable (c05..c14 vs c00..c09),
      triggering a flushable ingest. Verifies MemtableOverlappingFiles==1,
      MemTable.Count==3, no WAL bytes written, flush uses the ingest-as-flush
      path, ingested values win for overlapping keys (higher seqnum), and data
      survives reopen.
    
    Fixes #5734

commit 13eac2b800d36899bd3d2b4d9405c7dddee799ff
Author: sumeerbhola <sumeer@cockroachlabs.com>
Date:   Wed Mar 11 16:31:13 2026 -0400

    db: add cumulative flushable mem bytes metrics
    
    The admission control two-stage model (cockroachdb/cockroach#156880)
    needs cumulative flushable memtable byte metrics from Pebble to map
    memtable bytes to L0 flushed bytes. The previous thinking had been
    to map cumulative WAL bytes to L0 flushed bytes (we already were
    tracking all the relevant WAL metrics). However, with raft and state
    machine engine separation, the state machine engine has no WAL, and
    we need a modeling approach that will work for it.
    
    Add two new metrics:
    - Metrics.MemTable.CumulativeFlushableMemBytes: cumulative inuseBytes
      of all flushables that have been created, including the current
      mutable memtable.
    - FlushMetrics.FlushableMemBytesIn: cumulative inuseBytes consumed by
      flush operations.
    
    The cumulative counter is maintained by accumulating inuseBytes() when
    flushables become immutable (memtable rotation and large batch path).
    The value read at rotation time may undercount due to in-flight
    writers that called prepare() before rotation but have not finished
    applying; this is acceptable for a metric used in admission control
    heuristics.
    
    Also fix ingestedFlushable.inuseBytes() to return 0 instead of
    panicking, since ingested flushables do not have in-memory bytes.
    
    Informs https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/156880
    
    Co-Authored-By: roachdev-claude <roachdev-claude-bot@cockroachlabs.com>
